chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.
chapter_note: This chapter is heavily overlaid with editorial material. The first half (¶1-11) is almost entirely dialogue frame, Gospel citation, and anti-sectarian polemic — the editors use Jesus' parable as a proof-text and argue against 'the sects' using NT examples (Judas, Paul, the date palm). The substrate teaching emerges in the second half with the five-fold faculty mapping: consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind → cosmic beings/locations for both the good tree (ascending: holy church → Pillar of Glory → First Man → Third Ambassador → the Father) and the bad tree (descending: law of death → transmigration → gehenna → vessel → the lump). This systematic faculty-realm correspondence is the oldest layer. The chapter closes with a dualistic creedal assertion (the two trees did not arise from one another) wrapped in exhortation. The editorial fatigue pattern is confirmed: substrate vocabulary increases in the second half while frame/institutional vocabulary drifts upward. The 'taste' mappings (good tree → holy church/catechumens; bad tree → the sects) are editorial applications that reach outside the cosmic system into contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Purely formulaic opening marker. Introduces the chapter as the first question. No cosmological content.

Dialogue frame with Gospel citation (Matthew 7:17-20 parallel). 'As it is written in the Gospel, he says' — citation formula marks this as editorial. The parable entered this text via NT citation, not as pre-Mani substrate. 'We beseech you, our master' is standard disciple-question formula.
Continuation of disciple question. 'It is written [...] scriptures' — further citation framework. 'Mystery by mystery' — pedagogical formula. No cosmological substance to extract.

'The sects' — one side of the discussion reaches into the contemporary religious landscape. The editors present alternative interpretations of the parable. 'Composite earth' appears but within the sects' reported reasoning, not as substrate teaching.

Opens with full dialogue frame attribution ('Then speaks our master Manichaios, the apostle of greatness'). Substantive content discusses the sects' interpretations and introduces the date palm example — editorial polemic against literal readings. No substrate teaching extractable.

Very fragmentary. Continues the date palm discussion — fibres, branches, dust, sweet/bad qualities. This is editorial reasoning about the mixed nature of physical trees, arguing against literal identification. Not cosmological mapping.

NT narrative proof-text: Judas counted among the twelve, then Satan entered him. 'It is written about him' — citation formula. Used to illustrate the mixture principle through a scriptural example. The mixture doctrine is cosmological but the vehicle (Judas narrative) is editorial.
Continuation of Judas example. 'First they called him a good man' — editorial illustration of good-to-bad transformation in a composite being.

Paul example: persecutor → apostle (bad-to-good). 'It is written about Paul' — citation formula. 'The mingling' and 'mingled in all things' briefly touch cosmological vocabulary but function within the editorial argument about mixture in composite beings. The principle of mingling is substrate; its illustration through Paul is editorial.

Transitional paragraph: rejects 'the sects' explanation, promises Mani's true revelation. 'The saviour preached in the parable' — citation frame. 'What are these two trees?' — the question is cosmological but embedded in editorial transition and polemic.

Very fragmentary. 'How I will reveal to you' — first-person frame promise. 'The Father' and 'the Pillar' are cosmic entities but too fragmentary to extract as coherent teaching. Transitional passage leading into the substrate proper.

paragraphs.core_text: ... the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [ ... ] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.
paragraphs.temporal_note: High substrate vocabulary (37.93). 'Intellectuals cloaked upon its body' — faculty-body correspondence, both sides within cosmic system. 'Light elements mingled, compounded in the totality' — systematic description of cosmic mixture. Clear oldest layer. Impersonal, descriptive voice.

Seam flag confirmed. Maps the tree's 'fruit' to 'Jesus the Splendour, the father of all the apostles' and its 'taste' to 'the holy church, in her teachers and her [...] the catechumens.' While Jesus the Splendour is a cosmic figure in Manichaean cosmology, 'father of all the apostles' crosses into institutional territory, and 'the holy church, teachers, catechumens' is clearly institutional application — one side of the mapping reaches into the organized church.
Minimal fragment with bridge connective 'Behold, this is.' Summary/demonstrative statement. Too brief to classify with confidence but the connective pattern is editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] Its consideration is the holy church. [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [ ... ] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed '[ ... ] I reveal to you [ ... ]' — dialogue frame attribution. Note: 'Its consideration is the holy church' preserved for enumeration integrity despite institutional vocabulary. Four of five mappings are clearly cosmos→cosmos (Pillar of Glory, First Man, Third Ambassador, the Father). The 'consideration → holy church' mapping may be editorial substitution or may use 'holy church' in its cosmic sense (gathered light particles). Uncertainty flagged.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core five-fold faculty mapping: intellectual faculties → cosmic beings/locations. Ship of living waters = moon ship; ship of living fire = sun ship. This is systematic correspondential teaching — domain mapped onto domain. The ascending hierarchy (church → Pillar → First Man → Ambassador → Father) matches the ascent sequence in ¶17. High substrate score (43.82) confirms.

Seam flag confirmed. Very high institutional vocabulary (29.73): 'alms', 'catechumens', 'purified in the holy church.' This is editorial extension applying the ascending faculty teaching to Manichaean church practices — the process of purification through alms-giving. One side of the mapping reaches into institutional practice.

paragraphs.core_text: It is consideration that shall [ ... ] they shall be raised up [ ... ] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure substrate: the ascending sequence through five faculties mapped to cosmic beings and locations. Ship of the night = moon, ship of the day = sun. The process is systematic and impersonal — it describes HOW souls ascend through the cosmic hierarchy. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. 'The God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory' — cosmological titles for the Father. No frame, citation, or editorial markers.

Summary/transition echoing Gospel parable language: 'This is the good tree that shall give good fruit.' Connects the substrate teaching back to the proof-text framework. 'The entire life and light for ever' has cosmological resonance but functions as editorial summary. 'It is blessed' is possibly exhortative.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] bad [ ... ] happen in [ ... ] from [ ... ] also [ ... ] the way that it is [ ... ] the good tree [ ... ] of the fire [ ... ] they are the ruling-power [ ... ] heaven and the wheel [ ... ] they are the five fleshes that walk [ ... ] fruit [ ... te]aching as of error, the mystery that [ ... wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very fragmentary but identifiable vocabulary is cosmological: 'the ruling-power', 'heaven and the wheel', 'the five fleshes' (the five types of beings in the kingdom of Darkness), 'Satan appointed in the world' (cosmic narrative of Satan establishing error in the physical cosmos). Describes the bad tree's cosmic nature. Both sides of identifiable mappings stay within the cosmic system. Substrate score 9.64 despite fragmentation.

Maps bad tree's taste to 'these evil people, the sects [...] bound in law after law, they and their teachers [...] the law of death.' One side of the mapping reaches into the contemporary religious landscape — 'the sects' and 'their teachers' are the editor's identified opponents. Parallel to ¶13's institutional mapping of the good tree's taste. 'The law of death' and 'souls of death' are cosmological terms used to characterize contemporary groups.

Editorial summary: 'the one that our master called' — dialogue frame attribution; 'in the scriptures' — citation frame; 'all the sects know it' — polemic. Connects the teaching back to the Gospel parable and polemicizes against the sects.

paragraphs.core_text: The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death. Its counsel is transmigration [ ... ] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [ ... ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [ ... ] vessel. Its mind is the [ ... ] the lump, the last bond, the [ ... ], they that Satan cast away [ ... ] the great [ ... ] and they fall [ ... ] the Darkness [ ... ] all [ ... ] and they take away [ ... ] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [ ... ] the fruit of Darkness, the one that they [ ... ] for ever and ever [ ... ] his face [ ... ] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed '[ ... I will] reveal to you and you [ ... ]' (dialogue frame). Removed 'from which the sects take instruction' after 'the law of death' (editorial bridge — maps cosmic concept to contemporary sects' behavior, one side reaches outside the cosmic system).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core five-fold faculty mapping for the bad tree, exact negative counterpart to ¶15. Descending hierarchy: law of death → transmigration → gehenna/furnaces → vessel → the lump (the last bond). The cosmic eschatology (swallowed into the lump, bound in the fruit of Darkness, no repentance) describes terminal cosmic destiny. Both sides of the faculty-realm mappings stay within the cosmic system. Substrate score 10.06.
Summary frame: 'this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you.' First-person retrospective. Very fragmentary. No extractable cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] which lies in its good earth [ ... life] and light; as death and Darkness do not exist [ ... ] Also, the bad tree is Matter [ ... wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [ ... ] Darkness and death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Concerning this [ ... ] and my beloved ones [ ... ] them in truth, it being changed from [ ... ]' (exhortation address — 'my beloved ones' is community address formula). Removed 'it, I understand it alone among the [ ... ]' (first-person editorial claim of unique understanding).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Dualistic cosmological identification: good tree in good earth (life, light; death and Darkness absent) vs. bad tree = Matter in bad earth (Darkness, death). This is the semi-creedal substrate assertion Gardner identifies. 'The bad tree is Matter' — direct ontological identification, both sides within the cosmic system. Exhortation score 6.85 reflects the 'my beloved ones' address.

paragraphs.core_text: He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one! The person who can separate them out may go up to the aeon of light
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Blessed is every one [ ... ]' (exhortation beatitude formula — editorial devotional wrapper). Removed '[ ... as I have] revealed it to you' (dialogue frame — first-person retrospective).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core dualistic creedal assertion: 'they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one!' — this is the absolute dualism teaching. The two principles are eternally separate, not derived from each other. 'May go up to the aeon of light' — eschatological promise tied to understanding. The teaching IS the creedal core; the beatitude wrapper is editorial devotional closure.

paragraphs.core_text: bad fruit did not arise from it [ ... ]; but whoever will not separate out [ ... ] from one another, he falls to the land of Darkness [ ... ] until he arrives at the [ ... ]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'And he sees [ ... ]' (continuation of exhortation frame from ¶25's beatitude — 'he' refers to the 'blessed one').
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of dualistic teaching: 'bad fruit did not arise from it' — cosmological assertion about the good tree's nature. 'He falls to the land of Darkness' — cosmic eschatological consequence. Both sides within the cosmic system. Low substrate score (4.35) but the identifiable content is cosmological.

Pure exhortation closure. 'Blessed is whoever can believe!' — beatitude formula. 'For ever and ever' — devotional closing formula. Seam flag confirmed: this extends the preceding teaching sequence with devotional application. High exhortation score (36.36).
